gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2, which our page and ChatGPT both recommend, may ship with AC-ECO mode turned on, a setting that cuts AC output after a stretch of low or no load, so the fridge could lose power during a compressor off-cycle unless the shopper turns AC-ECO off (wording seen only in search snippets; the manual text is not yet read).
standout_why: I read the four rival pages ChatGPT cited that would load. theoutagebrief.com/2026/10/22 only estimates runtimes at 85% inverter efficiency and gives an estimated compressor surge of 750–1,200 W. homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/refrigerator gives a 1,000 W startup figure from Champion and a 67 W average draw. wattpowerstation.com/guides/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator gives CNET's 12.58–38.58 h fridge runtimes and the station's own draw (12–74 W), and covers only UPS pass-through. None of them mention ECO, auto-off, AC timeout or any low-load shutoff. The Yahoo/CNET lab page returned 403, so I could not check it. They do cover the other mechanisms (surge and inverter overhead), so the auto-off point is the only new mechanism. It is a setup step, not a reason to pick a different unit, so it scores 2 rather than 3.
decides: This confirms the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 pick on one condition. The 24-hour plan only works with AC-ECO turned off, and auto-off settings on the other candidates (Anker's outlet timeout, EcoFlow's AC timeout) should be set to never. The page should carry this as a required setup step next to each pick. It cannot go on the page until the Elite 200 V2 manual text is read and quoted.
